thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: elevated 5xx + timeouts on /v1/generate (us-west-2). Error rate ~10x baseline, gateway 504/502 spikes starting ~08:10 UTC. Paging prod-oncall.

maria: I'm on. seeing dashboard alert too. query for batcher/scheduler queue depths and gateway 5xx traces.

ajay: pulling metrics now — looks like the batcher queue length jumped and stayed high. some nodes showing queue_size > 4k for the batcher service.

lena: linking the histogram for request wait time: p95 went from 30ms -> 3.2s, p99 ~ 8-12s for placement wait. logs show repeated "batcher_hold_time_exceeded" and gateway 504s.

ajay: paste of `kubectl logs` from an affected batcher pod:```
[2026-03-15T08:11:02Z] INFO batcher: enqueue req id=abc123 size=512 tokens wait=1200ms
[2026-03-15T08:11:05Z] WARN batcher: batch formation delayed, queue_size=4120
[2026-03-15T08:11:07Z] ERROR batcher: head_of_line_block detected, oldest_wait_ms=18450
[2026-03-15T08:11:09Z] ERROR runtime: model call timed out after 30s, upstream 5xx
```

maria: head_of_line blocking — long-wait requests at front preventing progress, whole scheduler starves. possible cause: large requests or stalled GPU kernels. check per-request token counts.

kevin: checking ingress traces for a sample of failed requests — many of the timed-out requests are large context runs ( > 4k tokens ) hitting the same partition. also seeing KV cache growth on those GPUs around same time.

lena: impact assessment — ~1.8% of overall traffic in us-west-2 sees 5xx/504, but certain customer cohorts (batching-heavy) hit 12% failure. generating incident bridge and notifying sales/success for impacted customers.

incident-bot: Incident bridge created: https://zoom.company/incident-2360456789 by maria

maria: quick mitigation checklist: 1) enable fallback route to smaller model for gateway path /v1/generate 2) reduce batcher max_wait_ms to shorten head-of-line hold 3) evict oldest requests > 15s wait 4) drain/replace affected batcher pods 5) notify customers. I'll run 1+2 now.

ajay: running the config change to batcher:```bash
curl -X POST https://controlplane/api/v1/configs/batcher -d '{"max_wait_ms":25, "max_batch_size":16}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***'
```

devops-bot: config change accepted, rolling update triggered for batcher config across pool-id=usw2-batcher-1

maria: enabling route fallback to redwood-small-v2 for non-enterprise tier:```json
{"route":"/v1/generate","condition":"tier!=enterprise","fallback_model":"redwood-small-v2"}
```

kevin: also flipping an emergency circuit-breaker for long-running requests at gateway (timeout -> 12s) to reduce amplifier effect, and setting upstream retry disabled for these paths.

lena: eviction script to drop oldest waiting requests (>15s) queued on batcher pool; starting now.```bash
scripts/evict_old_queue.sh --pool usw2-batcher-1 --older-than 15s --dry-run=false
```

ajay: restarting 3 highest-queue batcher pods (rotational) — cordon, drain, restart to clear possible stuck kernels. rolling restart in progress.

maria: quick customer note draft for CS: "We are experiencing elevated timeouts and 5xx in us-west-2 due to a scheduler/batcher queue backlog causing head-of-line blocking. We have enabled temporary fallbacks and reduced batch wait thresholds to mitigate. Working on full recovery, will update in 30m." @product-oncall please review.

product-oncall: looks fine, send to impacted customers list A and B, include temporary mitigations and ETA 30–45m.

kevin: metrics after config changes: queue depth dropping from 4k -> 800 in 6 minutes. gateway 5xx rate down from 10x -> ~1.6x baseline. p95 wait now ~120ms.

maria: good trend. leaving the emergency fallback in place for 1 hour, batcher config change to remain until postmortem decisions. keeping bridge open for now.

lena: adding to incident log: probable root contributors: unusually high fraction of large-context requests concentrated on a few batcher shards, KV cache growth causing slower kernel evictions, and batcher parameters allowing long waits producing head-of-line blocking.

ajay: creating internal bug for smarter hot-shard routing and early evict heuristics: BUG-12568. linking profiling artifacts: https://internal-reports/12568/prof

maria: handoff — I'm stepping out in 20m. kevin will be primary responder for next shift. kevin, please watch queue depths and customer escalations. action items for oncall: 1) monitor 5xx and p95, 2) if queue > 2k for > 10m, escalate to infra-sre immediately, 3) coordinate with product for rollback of fallback if regressions arise.

kevin: ack, taking over. I'll keep bridge open and update every 15m. logging all actions to the incident timeline.

devops-bot: rolling restart completed for 3 pods in usw2-batcher-1.

lena: customer impact update: total affected requests ~1.2% after mitigations; 3 paid customers reported degraded service — CS ticket created and onboarding to the bridge.

maria: thanks team. postmortem owner: lena. initial timeline + logs collected. we should consider a short-term mitigation plan: auto-fallback when a shard queue exceeds X and a long-term fix: hot-shard rebalancer + KV eviction tuning.

kevin: standing by. metrics are stable for now. leaving incident open for postmortem items. :white_check_mark:
